pages.title: Choose what can move
pages.text: An Output Item Node takes items out of its attached inventory; an Input Item Node inserts them.$(br2)Choose $(thing)Whitelist$() to allow matching samples, or $(thing)Blacklist$() to exclude them. An empty whitelist allows nothing; an empty blacklist allows everything.$(br2)Double-click player-inventory items to copy samples; double-click samples to clear them. Check both ends.

pages.title: Matching options
pages.text: $(thing)Tags$() allows equivalent materials through shared tags, such as planks or ingots/silver.$(br2)$(thing)NBT$() requires matching item data, such as enchantments or custom names. $(thing)Damage$() separately requires matching durability.$(br2)These options apply in both list modes. A blacklist rejects an item if it matches any sample with the selected options.

pages.title: Processing categories
pages.text: Input Nodes also offer a $(thing)Category$(): All items, Smeltable, Wood, Ingots or Other. It is an additional condition on the sample filter. Use an empty blacklist to accept the entire category, or add exclusions such as generator fuel.$(br2)Smeltable checks current furnace recipes, including datapacks. Wood, Ingots and Other exclude smeltables, so a full smelter leaves its backlog in the source. Smeltable logs become charcoal; non-smeltable planks go to Wood. Ingots uses Forge ingot tags; Other accepts the remaining items.

pages.title: Combine the two filters
pages.text: An item must pass $(thing)both$() Category and the sample filter. Category does not replace Whitelist/Blacklist.$(br2)Example: choose $(thing)Smeltable$(), $(thing)Blacklist$() and leave the samples empty to accept every furnace ingredient. Add a sand sample to accept all smeltables except sand.$(br2)With Whitelist, only listed items within that category pass. Tags, NBT and Damage affect sample matching; they do not broaden the category. An empty whitelist still accepts nothing.

pages.title: Colored conditions
pages.text: The row below the title controls when the node can work.$(br2)Both $(thing)Positive$() selectors require their chosen sensor colors to be on. Both $(thing)Negative$() selectors require their colors to be off. Every selected condition must hold.$(br2)A gray X leaves a condition unused. See $(l:ariente:automation/sensors)Refill with Sensors$(/l) for signal setup.

pages.title: Send useful batches
pages.text: The Output Node’s $(thing)Batch$() setting is the minimum transfer size, from 1 to 64. Single arrows change it by 1; double arrows change it by 8. A setting of 64 waits for a whole stack. Large batches use less flux per item.$(br2)Add a Round Robin Node behind an Output Node to rotate batches among eligible destinations.$(br2)If transfers stall, check batch availability, destination space, both filters and required conditions.
